query_text: Make a web app that feels like a proper hall of fame for our company's awards and industry recognition — the kind of thing you'd actually be proud to show a client, with each award displayed like it genuinely means something, maybe organized by year on one side and category on the other, so nothing just sits there looking like a footnote.

Build a web app for a supply chain transparency and sustainability reporting microsite that feels like the company actually believes in what it's publishing — a site with real character, where the sourcing stories and sustainability numbers are laid out in a way that feels honest and considered, with a section that lets visitors trace the journey of materials and another that shows the annual progress report in a clean, readable format, the kind of thing that earns trust rather than just checks a box.

Need a web app that works as a press resources and media kit download portal with a soul to it — the kind of place a journalist actually enjoys coming back to, where brand assets, press releases, and executive photos all have their own proper home and feel curated rather than dumped in a folder, and reporters can find exactly what they need browsing from a desktop browser without having to email anyone.

Need a web app for a customer referral reward program enrollment site that actually feels worth joining — something that shows the rewards clearly and makes the sign-up feel like a moment, with a place where people can track their referral progress and see what they've earned, the kind of site that makes the program feel like it was designed with taste and not just slapped together to hit a quota.

Create a web app for a corporate awards nomination and public voting platform that carries some genuine ceremony — a browser-based tool where nominees get their own proper spotlight rather than just a row in a table, and the voting feels like it means something, with a clear tally visible to the public and a nomination form that feels considered and not just a generic form dump.

Need a web app that works as a product ecosystem and partner integration showcase with the kind of identity that makes you feel like these partnerships were chosen with care — a site for desktop browsers where each partner and integration gets its own real presence, organized so visitors can explore by what they need rather than just scrolling through a wall of logos, and the overall feel is something you'd actually be proud to link to.

Make a web app that's a virtual brand showroom and immersive experience tour with a real sense of place — a browser-based tool where visitors feel like they're walking through a curated space rather than clicking through a slideshow, each product or brand moment given room to breathe, with a guided tour path and the option to explore freely, the kind of thing that makes the brand feel alive rather than just described.

A cause marketing pledge and charity campaign app for desktop browsers that feels like something people will actually want to be part of — a site where visitors can make a pledge, see the running total of what the community has committed together, and explore the story behind the cause, the kind of tool that gives the campaign a genuine heartbeat rather than just a donate button tacked on to the homepage.

Need a web app that's a multi-brand corporate portfolio showcase site with the kind of taste that lets each brand actually have its own personality within the same space — a browser-based tool where visitors can explore each brand on its own terms, with a clean overview on the home screen and then a proper deep-dive for each one, so the whole thing feels like an intentional family rather than a random collection.

Create a web app that's an influencer seeding program application portal with enough character that creators actually want to apply — a site for desktop browsers where the program's identity comes through clearly, the application form feels thoughtful and specific about what kind of partnership is on offer, and applicants can see what past collaborations have looked like, so the whole thing feels like an invitation rather than a job posting.

Need a web app for wholesale pricing and bulk order management that just handles the whole mess in one place — a browser-based tool where I can set different price tiers for different customers, put in a big order without having to recalculate everything by hand, and see all the pending bulk orders at a glance without digging through spreadsheets, so I stop wasting half my day on stuff that should be automatic.

Need a web app that's an enterprise employee directory and org chart tool that actually makes it fast to find who you need — a browser-based tool where I can search by name or team, see how reporting lines connect without having to ask HR, and pull up someone's contact info and role in two clicks, because right now tracking down the right person takes forever and I'm tired of it.

Make a web app for corporate compliance training and policy management that takes the pain out of keeping everyone up to date — a browser-based tool where employees can find the current policies, complete their required training without hunting around, and managers can see who still needs to finish their certification, because right now tracking all of this is a spreadsheet nightmare and somebody always slips through.

Build a web app for commercial credit application and financing that removes all the back-and-forth of a paper process — a browser-based tool where a business can fill out their credit application, upload the required documents, and track where their request is in the review process without having to call anyone, so the whole thing moves faster and stops getting stuck in someone's inbox.

Need a web app that's an enterprise product catalog and price configurator in one — a browser-based tool where a sales rep can browse the full product lineup, pick the options and quantities for a specific customer, and get the right price calculated on the spot, because right now they have to check three different places and do math themselves, which takes forever and produces mistakes.

Create a web app that's a corporate annual report and shareholder communication site that makes the financial information actually readable — a browser-based tool where shareholders can find the year's highlights, dig into the financial details without wading through a PDF, and see key metrics clearly, because right now investors have to download a huge document just to answer a basic question and nobody has time for that.

Create a web app that's a B2B sales pipeline tracker with enough CRM connection to keep the team on the same page — a browser-based tool where each deal's stage is clear at a glance, contact notes are right there next to the opportunity, and I can see which accounts need follow-up this week without having to open five different tabs, because the current situation is just chaos.

Make a web app for scheduling executive interviews during talent acquisition that stops the endless email chains — a browser-based tool where candidates can pick from available time slots, the hiring manager's calendar is reflected accurately, and confirmation goes out automatically, because right now coordinating three or four senior people for a single interview takes days of back-and-forth that nobody has time for.

Create a web app for booking corporate ESG compliance audit appointments that gets rid of the scheduling chaos — a browser-based tool where the right auditor slots are visible, a company can pick a time that works, fill in the basic info about what needs to be reviewed, and get a confirmation without anyone having to chase emails, because right now setting up one of these audits is way harder than it should be.

A quarterly review meeting scheduler app for key accounts, browser-based and usable from a desktop, that takes the hassle out of coordinating these sessions — a tool where account managers can see which clients are due for a review, propose times based on everyone's availability, and send the invitation without having to do it all manually in their calendar, because chasing these meetings is a job unto itself and most of them end up being scheduled late.

Need a web app for booking enterprise ERP demo and evaluation sessions that cuts out all the friction — a browser-based tool where prospects can pick a time slot, specify what they need to see in the demo, and confirm the booking without going through a sales rep just to get a time on the calendar, because right now the gap between someone asking for a demo and actually getting one scheduled is way too long.

Make a web app for scheduling press and analyst briefing appointments that makes it easy for journalists and analysts to get time with the right person — a browser-based tool where they can see which spokesperson or subject matter expert is available, pick a slot, and describe what they need the briefing to cover, so the PR team spends less time playing calendar tennis and more time actually preparing.

Make a web app for booking commercial insurance underwriting consultations that takes the confusion out of the process — a browser-based tool where a business owner can pick a time to meet with an underwriter, describe the coverage they're looking at, and get a reminder before the appointment, because right now just figuring out how to get in front of the right person involves way too many calls that go nowhere.

Create a web app for booking enterprise data proof-of-concept engagement sessions that makes it easy for a prospect to get one actually scheduled — a browser-based tool where they can pick a date, describe their use case and what they want to test, and confirm the engagement without needing to go through five people, because right now the process of setting up a POC is so slow that some deals just die waiting.

Build a web app for regulatory compliance refresher training and recertification that keeps everything organized in one place — a browser-based tool where employees can see which courses they still need to complete, work through the material at their own pace, and get their recertification confirmed when they pass, and managers can see a simple list of who is up to date and who still needs to finish, so nobody misses a deadline because the system was confusing.

Need a web app that tracks language learning progress for every employee across the whole company, where managers can see which staff have completed which courses and what their current proficiency level is, and there's a sidebar listing all departments so you can drill into a team and see everyone's status at a glance.

A corporate innovation learning hub for desktop browsers where employees can browse a library of curated resources — articles, videos, case studies — organised by theme, bookmark the ones they want to revisit, and see a list of upcoming internal workshops they can sign up for.

Build a web app for our company's internal executive education portal where senior staff can enroll in leadership courses, track which modules they've finished, and see a clear list of what's still left to complete, with a separate area showing upcoming live sessions they can register for.

A high-potential talent tracker for desktop browsers where HR can log each person's current role, their target future role, and the specific learning steps they need to hit along the way, with a checklist on each person's profile showing which development milestones are done and which are still pending.

Create a workplace safety training manager as a web app where staff can see a list of all required safety certifications, mark which ones they've completed, and get a reminder when a certificate is about to expire, with a separate view for team leads to check their whole team's compliance status at once.

Need a product academy web app for our enterprise clients where they can browse a structured list of courses about our products, track their progress through each one, and get a certificate when they finish, with a sidebar that organises everything by product line so they can quickly find what's relevant to them.

Create a customer support forum web app where users can post questions and browse answers from other customers, and if nobody in the community can help, there's an easy way to flag the thread so a real expert gets notified and steps in — the whole thing lives in a browser and the left side shows topic categories to navigate around.

A study group platform for professional certification candidates that runs in a browser, where people preparing for the same exam can join a shared space, post study notes and practice questions, and see a list of active group sessions they can jump into — with each group organised by the specific certification it focuses on.

Make a company knowledge base wiki as a web app where employees can write and edit articles together, and anyone reading a page can leave a comment or highlight a specific paragraph and stick a note on it so others can see what their colleagues thought about that part.

Make a customer referral tracker as a web app where we can give each existing customer a unique referral link, see a list of who they've referred and whether those referrals actually signed up, and the tracker automatically keeps a running total of how many successful referrals each person has made so we know who to reward.

Create a web app where companies in the same industry can share their performance numbers and see how they stack up against everyone else — you pick which metrics you want to contribute, submit your data, and then get a comparison showing where you sit relative to the group average, with filters to narrow it down by company size or region.

Need a hackathon project showcase website where participants can post their project with a short description and a link to their demo, other attendees can browse all the submissions in a big grid, and there's a way to connect with teammates or people working on similar ideas right from the project listing.

Need a web app for managing local brand chapters and meetups, where chapter organizers can list upcoming events in their city, members can sign up for events they want to attend, and there's a directory showing all the active chapters around the country so people can find the one closest to them.

A brand compliance checker tool for desktop browsers where you upload a marketing file and it goes through and flags anything that uses the wrong colours, wrong fonts, or wrong logo version, then gives you a clear list of every issue it found so you can fix them one by one instead of hunting through the file yourself.

Make a web app that shows me all our API usage in one place — which teams are using which APIs, how much of their quota they've burned through, and whether anyone is getting close to the limit so we can deal with it before something breaks.

Build a workforce scheduling tool as a web app where managers can set up the weekly shift rota for their team, staff can request to swap a shift with a colleague, and the manager gets a simple approval queue to sign off on swap requests so nothing slips through without anyone noticing.

A browser-based NPS survey tool where you can write a short customer satisfaction survey, send it out, and then see all the responses collected in one place with a simple score summary and a list of the open-ended comments people left, so you can actually read what they said without digging through a spreadsheet.

A vendor invoice portal for desktop browsers where our finance team can upload invoices, match them against what we expected to pay, and if something doesn't line up there's a simple way to flag it as a dispute and add a note explaining the issue so the vendor knows exactly what's wrong.

Make a data access request tracker as a web app where employees can submit a request to get access to a specific dataset, the request goes to the right approver automatically, and everyone involved can see the current status of each request in a simple list — pending, approved, or rejected — so nothing just disappears into someone's inbox.

Create a product roadmap voting tool as a web app where team members can submit feature ideas, everyone gets a set number of votes to put toward the ideas they care most about, and the list automatically sorts by most votes so leadership can see at a glance which things the team actually wants built next.

Make a startup awards showcase wall as a web app that actually feels like something worth sharing — not just a bland list, but a proper display where each award has its own moment, with the year it was won and what it was for, and the whole thing has the kind of quiet confidence that makes visitors take the company seriously.

Build a product media gallery for desktop browsers where we can show off screenshots and demo videos in a way that feels polished and intentional — grouped by feature area, with a clean layout that lets the product speak for itself rather than getting buried under clutter.

Make a startup accelerator portfolio site as a web app that feels like it has real personality — a place where each cohort has its own section, you can browse all the companies that came through the program, and alumni can be found by batch year or industry, the kind of site that makes you proud to say you were part of this.

A thought leadership blog and resource library for desktop browsers that actually has a point of view — articles are front and centre with a strong editorial feel, downloadable guides are organised so people can find what they need fast, and the whole thing reads like it was built by people who have something real to say.

Create a use case library web app for our SaaS product where each industry vertical gets its own dedicated section with real stories about how companies in that space use the product, and visitors can filter by their industry and see the examples most relevant to them, so it feels like the product was made specifically for whoever is reading it.
